title: About GAMSA
intro: Who made this site and why, what is on it, how the pages are written, checked and kept up to date, and what to do if something is wrong.

sections.h: Who made this site and why
paras: Theodore South, BPharm (Hons), writes and checks every page and keeps the site up to date.

Theodore is registered with the Pharmacy Board of Australia. You can check any pharmacist's registration on the [Ahpra register of practitioners](https://www.ahpra.gov.au/Registration/Registers-of-Practitioners.aspx) by searching their name.

GAMSA was established by Theodore South, a registered pharmacist in Adelaide, in response to two recurring problems: a lack of clear, accessible information on gender-affirming hormone therapy, and repeated shortages of the medicines used for it and alongside it. It exists to fill those gaps for trans and gender diverse people in South Australia, and for the families, friends and clinicians who support them. It brings reliable information together in one place, written in plain language and referenced to the Australian standards of care, the Product Information, the PBS and the TGA. GAMSA is independent, non-commercial and free to use. Built for the community, by a member of the community.
With special thanks to Theodore's brother, Tobin, for providing the software tools that help build and check this site.
The pages describe how medicines are generally used. They are not advice for one person. Please speak with your prescriber or pharmacist about your own care.
bullets: People who take, or are thinking about, gender-affirming hormone therapy, and their families and supporters.
Pharmacists, nurses, GPs and other prescribers who want a clear, sourced reference. See [For clinicians](#/clinicians).
**Medicines:** a page for each medicine, with doses, how to use it, PBS costs and today's supply status. See [Medicines A–Z](#/medicines).

**Supply:** shortage status from the TGA, checked every morning, [pharmacy stock reports](#/pharmacy-reports) from pharmacists, and [stock seen by the community](#/sightings). Community reports are not checked, so ring the pharmacy before you go.

**Family and carers:** a page for [parents and carers of under-18s](#/parents), a guide to [helping an adult with their medicines](#/ally-guide), and [Words and terms](#/terminology), a plain-language guide to words about gender.

**Clinicians:** [Starting hormones: a GP guide](#/starting-hormones), the [Clinician reference](#/clinician-guide), the [injection training package](#/med/testosterone-undecanoate#injection-training) and [shortage alerts](#/alerts) as a feed you can subscribe to.
**Guides to print:** checklists, logs, forms and guides, free to download from [Guides to print](#/downloads).
**Easy Read:** short guides in easy words, with pictures. See [Easy Read guides](#/easy).

paras: GAMSA is independent and non-commercial, and it is free to use. It has no funding, no advertising and no sponsors. It is not linked to any clinic, pharmacy, drug company, government body or advocacy group. No brand or company pays to be mentioned, and no brand is promoted over another.

bullets: Clinical pages are based on the Australian standards of care (AusPATH), the Australian Product Information for each medicine, the PBS, the TGA and published research. Each page lists its sources under References.
Pages use plain words and short sentences. They describe how medicines are generally used. They are not advice for one person.

PBS Schedule information is reproduced with permission of the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing. It is PBS information, not GAMSA's own, and it is shown with the date it was extracted from www.pbs.gov.au.

**AI-assisted drafting:** some text is first drafted with an AI writing tool. A pharmacist checks every statement against its source before it goes on the site. Nothing is published without that check.

paras: Supply and PBS figures update automatically from the TGA and the PBS. Everything else changes only after the pharmacist has read the new information and checked it against its source.
bullets: A page is reviewed again when AusPATH, a Product Information, the PBS or a TGA safety notice changes.
Each medicine page shows the date it was last reviewed.
Dated changes to the information on this site are listed on [What's changed](#/changes).

figure.title: How GAMSA stays current
figure.alt: Three columns: what GAMSA checks every morning, every week and every month
figure.long: Three regular checks: every morning, every week and every month.

cols.head: Every morning
items: Supply status is read from the TGA shortages database for every medicine on this site.
The supply page and the shortage alerts feed are rebuilt from it.

cols.head: Every week
items: Guideline, safety and policy pages are checked for anything new, such as AusPATH, the NHMRC, TGA safety alerts and PBS news.
New items are listed for the pharmacist to read. No written information changes until the pharmacist has checked it.

cols.head: Every month
items: PBS prices, Safety Net amounts, brand premiums and listings are read just after the PBS changes on the 1st.
The date each Product Information was last changed, and links to other sites, are checked.

figure.note: When a source changes, the page is reviewed again by the pharmacist and the change is listed on What's changed.
figure.caption: How the regular checks on this site are scheduled.
figure.easyTitle: How we keep the website up to date

easy.text: Every morning we check which medicines are hard to get.
Every week we look for new health advice.
Every month we check prices and links.
A pharmacist checks new health advice before we change the website.

paras: The Aboriginal flag and the Torres Strait Islander flag are shown with the Acknowledgement of Country at the foot of every page. The Torres Strait Islander flag was designed by the late Mr Bernard Namok and is used with the permission of the Torres Strait Island Regional Council.
If something is wrong, out of date or missing, [send feedback](#/feedback), or email gamsaenquiries@gmail.com. Safety errors are fixed first.

Please send any complaint about this site through the [feedback form](#/feedback). It is the only way to make a complaint to GAMSA, so that every complaint is recorded and answered. If you are not satisfied with the reply, you can go to:
bullets: **Health and Community Services Complaints Commissioner (HCSCC SA)**: independent complaints about health services in South Australia, including pharmacists. [HCSCC website](https://www.hcscc.sa.gov.au/).

**Ahpra**: concerns about a registered pharmacist's practice or conduct. [How to raise a concern](https://www.ahpra.gov.au/Notifications/Concerned-about-a-health-practitioner.aspx), phone 1300 419 495.

**Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)**: privacy complaints, after you have complained to us first (see the [Privacy page](#/privacy)). [Privacy complaints](https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-complaints), phone 1300 363 992.

paras: Full details are on the [Accessibility page](#/accessibility).
bullets: **Aim:** WCAG 2.1 Level AA for all pages at gamsa.au.
**Status:** partly meets the aim. No independent audit has been done.
**Relies on:** HTML, CSS, JavaScript and WAI-ARIA.
**How it is checked:** every release is tested with automated tools (axe), in light and dark mode, with keyboard-only and zoom checks.
**Known gaps:** the PDFs are not fully tagged for screen readers; the same content is on the web pages.

**Spam check on forms:** the feedback and report forms use Cloudflare Turnstile to stop spam. It is outside our control. It may not work with some screen readers, voice control, switch access, older browsers or strict privacy settings. If it blocks you, email gamsaenquiries@gmail.com instead.
